Honorable Scott S. Harris 
Clerk of the Court 
Supreme Court of the United States 
1 First Street, NE 
Washington, DC 20543 

Re:  Luis Nieves et al.  v. Russell Bartlett, No. 17-117 4 

Dear Mr. Harris: 

The purpose of this letter is to request extensions of the briefing deadlines in 
Nieves et al.  v. Bartlett, No. 17- 1174, pursuant to Supreme Court Rule 30.4. Counsel for 
petitioners and for respondent are in agreement on the briefing deadlines proposed in this 
letter. 

Petitioners propose a one-week extension of the deadline for their opening merits 

brief. Undersigned counsel had to devote time to finishing two other appellate briefs in 
early July, so a one-week extension oftime will allow counsel to make up the time that 
had to be spent on other matters. Under Supreme Court Rule 25.1, the brief is currently 
due on August  13, 2018. The one-week extension would make the brief due on Monday, 
August 20, 2018. 

With the proposed extension of petitioners' merits brief deadline, respondent' s 

brief would be due on September 19, 2018. Respondent proposes a  13-day extension of 
time until October 2, 2018. This extension is requested due to respondent's counsel's 
unavailability from September 1 through 20, 2018. Petitioners' reply brief will then be 
due on November 1, 2018. With the understanding that oral argument in this case is 
tentatively scheduled for the December calendar, the proposed extensions will not result 
in the reply brief being filed  less than a week before oral argument (which Rule 25.3 
prohibits).

Honorable Scott S. Harris 
Extension of Briefing Deadline 

July 25, 2018 
Page 2 of2 

Thank you very much for your consideration of our request for extensions. Please 

do not hesitate to contact me with any questions or concerns about this request. 

Sincerely, 

JAHNA LINDEMUTH 
ATTORNEY GENERAL
